content:
Ishan: quick heads-up — after the kernel selection change (flash-attn2 fallback) and the quantization patch, we've started hitting OOMs from KV cache pressure during continuous batching. repros on a couple 4g nodes today.
Marie: ack. any numbers on when it trips?
Ishan: p50 throughput similar, p95 latency +18%, and memory spikes when batch windows accumulate >~1200 tokens. KV footprint climbs nonlinearly.
Tory: hmm, sounds like admission logic is letting batches form without accounting for kv-per-token growth after quantization. did we recompute avg_kv_per_token for the new kernel?
Ishan: not for the quantized trunk. current estimate is from fp16 runs: 42 bytes/token. quantized seems closer to 58-65 bytes/token in profiling.
Liu: can you paste the profiler sample?
Ishan: paste below (short):
```
profiler: sample 2026-03-12
model: rdx-7b-q4
kernel: flash-attn2
avg_tokens_in_window: 1348
avg_kv_bytes_per_token: 61
free_kv_bytes_before_admit: 192MB
predicted_batch_kv: 82MB
observed_peak_kv: 210MB -> OOM on ~4g tiles
```
Marie: ugh. so our admission token_budget formula is stale. current code: token_budget = max_tokens - queued_tokens - reserved_kernel_headroom. no kv factor.
Tory: proposal: compute token_budget_kv = floor((free_kv_bytes - safety_margin) / avg_kv_bytes_per_token) and then use min(token_budget_kv, token_budget_latency). safety_margin should be dynamic (like 15% + estimated concurrent_evictions).
Ishan: I prototyped that locally; it reduces a single-batch p99 spike but reduces batch size leading to throughput loss ~6% on some mixes. tradeoff seems acceptable vs OOM.
DevOpsBot: deploy-canary: eng-runtime/canary/rdx-7b-q4 -> started 2026-03-12T15:10Z
BuildBot: canary logs: 3 OOMs in first 20m before patch; 0 OOMs after adaptive token_budget applied (50m run).
Liu: we should also add early kernel fallback: if predicted_kv > fallback_threshold then route to kernel variant with smaller kv (fallback_kernel) or force smaller window. that may preserve throughput without full shedding.
Marie: yes. two levers: 1) kv-aware admission (soft cap) 2) kernel routing fallback (hard cap). add a jittered window to avoid synchronized shedding.
Tory: another idea: precompute per-model, per-kernel avg_kv_bytes_by_seq histogram and store a 95th percentile kv-per-token. use that for safety-critical customers.
Ishan: will add metrics: request.kv_bytes_est, batch.kv_predicted, admission.reason (kv_headroom/fallback/latency). also add alert if observed_kv > predicted_kv + 30% for 5m.
Marie: please also add an e2e perf test that runs quantized workloads with long prefixes (simulate chat history) so we don't regress silently.
Ishan: plan: 1) initial patch to admission: token_budget_kv with safety_margin 15% + 1MB constant 2) kernel fallback hook (configurable threshold) 3) instrument metrics/alerts 4) perf test and canary. I'll open PR today.
Liu: LGTM. please include a short doc blurb on why avg_kv_per_token increased after quantization (sparse kv layout + index packing changed).
Tory: one more: when admission reduces window, push a small burst delay (50-150ms) for subsequent admits to let background evictions finish. avoids oscillation.
Ishan: good call. will implement soft delay with exponential backoff if repeated rejects.
Marie: sgtm. thanks. if you want pairing on the perf test I can help.
Ishan: appreciate it — pairing later today. I'll tag you on the PR. :thumbsup:
DevOpsBot: canary report attached: no OOMs after changes in 1h run, p95 latency slightly higher but within SLOs.
BuildBot: created issue #4129 and linked PR draft.
Marie: closing loop — post-merge let's run a 24h soak on dedicated machines before ramp.
Tory: noted. also add a quick runbook: how to revert kernel fallback and how to temporarily tighten token_budget if we see regressions.
Ishan: agree. will add runbook steps to the PR description.
Liu: thanks all, nice rapid iteration.
Marie: thanks team!
